question.leadin: Albert Einstein turned down the presidency of this country.
question.text: Identify this country that declared independence in 1948 following the end of British rule in Mandatory Palestine. It is the only officially Jewish country in the world.
question.clue: This country began Operation Wrath of God in response to the Munich Olympics Massacre, in which eleven of its athletes died.

swap.text: The hajj, on which Mansa Musa gave away great amounts of gold, is a Muslim pilgrimage undertaken to this holiest city in Islam.
swap.clue: As its citizens prepared to execute a negotiator, the Pledge of the Tree was taken outside of its walls, leading it to promptly accept the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

question.leadin: In the weeks after this man was overthrown in a July 3, 2013 military coup, he was said to be in a "safe place" but had not made a public appearance.
question.text: Name this former President of the Muslim Brotherhood's political party, the Freedom and Justice Party, who was elected President of his nation in 2012, shortly after the downfall of Hosni Mubarak.
question.clue: This leader defeated the Salafist Nour party to win his first election.

swap.leadin: British possessions in Asia were referred to as "East of" this structure.
swap.text: Name this waterway that connected the Mediterrainian and Red Sea when it was completed in 1869.
swap.clue: The Straits of Tiran were opened during a conflict over this structure that led to Anthony Eden's resignation.

question.leadin: The Battle of Karbala occurred between the forces of one leader of this government, Yazid I ("yah-ZEED the first"), and the forces of Husayn ibn Ali ("hoo-SAYN ibn AH-lee").
question.text: Name this second Muslim caliphate which was founded by Muawiyah ("moo-AH-wee-yah"), succeeding the Rashidun ("RAH-shee-doon") caliphate. It was defeated by the later Abbasid caliphate at the Battle of the Zab River.
question.clue: Its forces under Marwan II lost the Battle of the Zab, and Charles Martel defeated Moorish forces under this dynasty at the Battle of Tours.

swap.text: The Battle of Hattin saw the capture of this man who succeeded Baldwin IV as King of Jerusalem. This man was taken prisoner along with his rival Raynald of Chatillon.
swap.clue: A more prominent position held by this ruler was obtained through his wife Sibylla in spite of the intrigues of Raymond III of Tripoli.

question.text: Assad is a major leader of this international Arab nationalist party that overthrew Nazim al-Kudsi in a 1963 coup. It was founded by Michel Aflaq.
question.clue: This party's regime carried out the 1982 Hama massacre against the Muslim Brotherhood during the presidency of Hafez al-Assad, a dictator from this party.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about continuing violence in the Middle East.
swap.text: In February Assad's regime began shelling this western city south of Hama and north of Damascus. Street fights between Sunnis and Alawites broke out in this city where almost half the uprising's deaths have occurred.

question.text: The hometown of Saddam Hussein, this city located ninety miles north of Baghdad was one of the last to fall to American forces.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the adoption of Islam in Africa.
swap.text: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded after Usman dan Fodio led several of these Islamic religious wars to unite Hausaland ("how-suh-land").
swap.clue: This concept names campaigns against Hausaland led by Fulanis like Usman dan Fodio of the Sokoto Caliphate.

question.leadin: This structure created a reservoir that is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world and is named for the leader who constructed it.
question.text: Name this structure designed by the Soviet Hydroproject Institute. The USSR funded the completion of this project after the United States pulled funding for it in response to its home country's formal recognition of China.
question.clue: In 1956 John Foster Dulles announced that the US was withdrawing funding, following the Soviets offering over one billion dollars in funding.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Fifth Crusade.
swap.text: The Fifth Crusade was fought against the Ayyubid ("AH-yoob-id") dynasty, which was founded by this sultan who defended Jerusalem during the Third Crusade. This sultan was famous for his rivalry with Richard the Lionheart.
swap.clue: This ruler was defeated at the Battle of Arsuf by his rival during a larger conflict in which that rival was able to retake control of Joffa.

question.leadin: Despite a rivalry with Uthman, this man sent his sons in a failed attempt to protect him from assassins.
question.text: Name this man who later became the fourth Rashidun Caliph.
question.clue: Some of this man's followers split off and formed the Kharijite sect following the battle of Siffin, which he fought against the man who would eventually replace him, Mu'awiya.

swap.leadin: This kingdom formed out of a revolt encouraged by the McMahon-Hussein correspondence.
swap.text: Identify this non-Jordan kingdom ruled by the Hashemite dynasty. It contained a strategically important railway dotted with Ottoman garrisons that was frequently attacked by local tribes.
swap.clue: This brief-lived kingdom on the west coast of the Arabian peninsula, conquered by the Kingdom of Nejd after the capture of Jidda.

question.text: After Gemayel's assassination, the IDF gave Phalangist militias access to a refugee camp and a Shia neighborhood in Beirut, resulting in this massacre that forced Ariel Sharon ("sha-ROHN") to resign as defense minister.
question.clue: Elie Hobeika's forces were able to carry on slaughtering people through the night thanks to flares fired from a third party, which led the Kahan Commission to declare the sitting Defense Minister "personally responsible."

swap.text: Ten years prior, Christians in this city were massacred by Muslims during an event known as The Events. Between 2012 and 2016, sites in this city such as its Citadel and nine historic gates were damaged by artillery fire.
swap.clue: A rebuilt version of the Ayyubid Palace of Glory is contained within a defensive structure used by Seleucus Nicator, this massive Citadel of this city, outside of which Tamerlane built a tower of 20,000 skulls after taking it from the Mamluks.

question.leadin: A Latin maxim beginning with the phrase "sit tibi copia" is inscribed in Rayonnant ("RYE-yoh-NAHN") Gothic style on the portico of this structure's great Gothic hall.
question.text: Name this structure originally built for the Mirdasid dynasty. T.E. Lawrence wrote that it was the "the best preserved and most wholly admirable" structure of its kind in the world.
question.answerHtml: Krak des Chevaliers (“krahk day shev-ah-L’YAY”) [or Crac de l’Hospital or Hisn al-Akrād; prompt on Krak; reject “Kerak”]
question.clue: Speaking of Baybars, in 1271 CE, he successfully launched a siege against this Crusader castle near Homs which had been built up by the Knights Hospitallers starting in 1140 CE under direction of Raymond II, Count of Tripoli.

swap.text: During Poland's 1968 crisis, a government campaign nominally targeting this ideology resulted in the expulsion of two-thirds of Poland's Jews. Theodor Herzl created a "congress" for this ideology in 1897.
swap.clue: That letter supporting this cause was written by Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour.

question.leadin: This mystic famously declared "I am the Truth," prompting allegations that he claimed to be divine.
question.text: Name this mystic who was crucified by the Abbasid Caliph Al-Muqtadir in 922.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a man sometimes called the father of sociology. FTPE.
swap.text: This 14th Century Tunisian-born scholar worked out of Fez, Cairo, and Grenada, and authored a thorough seven volume history of the Islamic world, the Kitab al-Ibar.
swap.clue: This thinker, a longtime judge in Cairo, was a strong proponent of the concept of assabiya, or social solidarity.
